<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="190.5mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 190.5 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-active { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-down { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-error { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-laser-disabled { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-link-10 { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-link-100 { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-link-100 { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-link-1000 { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-no-optic { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-no-optic { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-not-shutdown { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-on { --led-color: #2f7fe0; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-2-10gb-xp@'] .state-up { --led-color: #39b54a; }

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="190.5mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 190.5 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-active { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-down { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-error { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-no-optic { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-no-optic { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-on { --led-color: #2f7fe0; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m12-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-up { --led-color: #39b54a; }</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="190.5mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 190.5 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-active { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-disabled { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-down { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-error { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-no-xfp { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-no-xfp { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-on { --led-color: #2f7fe0; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-up { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-wan-phy { --led-color: #39b54a; }</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="190.5mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 190.5 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-oc192-xp-xfp@'] .state-active { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-oc192-xp-xfp@'] .state-down { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-oc192-xp-xfp@'] .state-error { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-oc192-xp-xfp@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-oc192-xp-xfp@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-oc192-xp-xfp@'] .state-laser-disabled { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-oc192-xp-xfp@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-oc192-xp-xfp@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-oc192-xp-xfp@'] .state-no-optic { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-oc192-xp-xfp@'] .state-no-optic { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-oc192-xp-xfp@'] .state-on { --led-color: #2f7fe0; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m2-oc192-xp-xfp@'] .state-up { --led-color: #39b54a; }</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="190.5mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 190.5 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-down { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-on { --led-color: #2f7fe0; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-sfp@'] .state-up { --led-color: #39b54a; }</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="190.5mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 190.5 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-activity { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-down { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-error { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-link-10 { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-link-10 { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-link-100 { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-link-100 { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-link-1000 { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-not-shutdown { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-on { --led-color: #2f7fe0; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m20-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-up { --led-color: #39b54a; }</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="190.5mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 190.5 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m4-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-active { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m4-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-disabled { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m4-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-down { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m4-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-error { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m4-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m4-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m4-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m4-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-no-xfp { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m4-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-no-xfp { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m4-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-on { --led-color: #2f7fe0; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m4-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-up { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m4-10gb-xp-xfp@'] .state-wan-phy { --led-color: #39b54a; }</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="190.5mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 190.5 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m48-1gb-xp-tx@'] .state-down { --led-color: #f5a623; }

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="193.0mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 193.0 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-active { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-active { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-amber { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-blue { --led-color: #2f7fe0; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-errored { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-errored { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-green { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-loopback { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-loopback { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-no-optic { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e10-100g-qsfp28@'] .state-no-optic { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="193.0mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 193.0 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-active { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-active { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-amber { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-blue { --led-color: #2f7fe0; }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-errored { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-green { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-loopback { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-loopback { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-no-optic { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e16-100g-sfp112@'] .state-no-optic { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="193.0mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 193.0 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e2-100g-qsfp28-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-active { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e2-100g-qsfp28-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-active { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e2-100g-qsfp28-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-amber { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e2-100g-qsfp28-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-blue { --led-color: #2f7fe0; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e2-100g-qsfp28-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-errored { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e2-100g-qsfp28-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-errored { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e2-100g-qsfp28-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-green { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e2-100g-qsfp28-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e2-100g-qsfp28-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e2-100g-qsfp28-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e2-100g-qsfp28-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-loopback { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e2-100g-qsfp28-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-loopback { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e2-100g-qsfp28-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="193.0mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 193.0 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/m5e8-100g-sfp112-2-800g-qdd@'] .state-active { --led-color: #39b54a; }

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="190.5mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 190.5 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>
  <g id="mda-impedance-panel" data-path="mda-impedance-panel" data-class="blank" data-behaviour="fills" data-ref="nokia/mda-impedance-panel@1:1.0.0" data-model="7750 SR classic MDA Impedance Panel" data-role="slot-blank" transform="translate(0,0)">

      <rect x="5.2" y="28.25" width="4.9" height="1.55" />
      <rect x="180.5" y="28.25" width="4.9" height="3.1" />
    </g>
    <g id="mda-impedance-panel--screw-left" data-path="mda-impedance-panel/screw-left" data-class="screw" data-z-cyl="1.6">
      <circle cx="7.6" cy="22.9" r="5.0" fill="#34373b" stroke="#1a1c1f" stroke-width="0.25" />

      <circle cx="182.9" cy="22.9" r="5.0" fill="#34373b" stroke="#1a1c1f" stroke-width="0.25" />

    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="193.0mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 193.0 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/me12-10-1gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me12-10-1gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-loopback { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me12-10-1gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-loopback { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me12-10-1gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me12-10-1gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-no-optic { --led-color: #f5a623; }

    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="193mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 193 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/me16-25gb-sfp28-2-100gb@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me16-25gb-sfp28-2-100gb@'] .state-loopback { --led-color: #f5a623; }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/me16-25gb-sfp28-2-100gb@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me16-25gb-sfp28-2-100gb@'] .state-no-optic { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me16-25gb-sfp28-2-100gb@'] .state-no-optic { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me16-25gb-sfp28-2-100gb@'] .state-on { --led-color: #2f6fdb; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me16-25gb-sfp28-2-100gb@'] .state-up { --led-color: #39b54a; }</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="193.0mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 193.0 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-activity { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-down { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-error { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-laser-disabled { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-loopback { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-loopback { animation: portrayal-blink 0.25s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-no-optic { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-no-optic { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-on { --led-color: #2f6fdb; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me2-100gb-cfp4@'] .state-up { --led-color: #39b54a; }</style>

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-200gb-cfp2-dco@'] .state-no-optic { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="193mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 193 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-activity { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-down { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-error { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-loopback { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-loopback { animation: portrayal-blink 0.25s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-no-optic { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-no-optic { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-on { --led-color: #2f6fdb; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me3-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-up { --led-color: #39b54a; }</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="193.0mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 193.0 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/me40-1gb-csfp@'] .state-activity { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me40-1gb-csfp@'] .state-activity { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me40-1gb-csfp@'] .state-amber { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me40-1gb-csfp@'] .state-blue { --led-color: #2f7fe0; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me40-1gb-csfp@'] .state-green { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me40-1gb-csfp@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me40-1gb-csfp@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me40-1gb-csfp@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me40-1gb-csfp@'] .state-loopback { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me40-1gb-csfp@'] .state-loopback { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me40-1gb-csfp@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me40-1gb-csfp@'] .state-no-optic { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me40-1gb-csfp@'] .state-no-optic { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="193mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 193 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-100gb-qsfp28@'] .state-activity { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-100gb-qsfp28@'] .state-down { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-100gb-qsfp28@'] .state-error { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-100gb-qsfp28@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-100gb-qsfp28@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-100gb-qsfp28@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-100gb-qsfp28@'] .state-loopback { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-100gb-qsfp28@'] .state-loopback { animation: portrayal-blink 0.25s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-100gb-qsfp28@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-100gb-qsfp28@'] .state-no-optic { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-100gb-qsfp28@'] .state-no-optic { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-100gb-qsfp28@'] .state-on { --led-color: #2f6fdb; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-100gb-qsfp28@'] .state-up { --led-color: #39b54a; }</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="193.0mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 193.0 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-10gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-activity { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-10gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-amber { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-10gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-blue { --led-color: #2f7fe0; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-10gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-error { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-10gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-green { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-10gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-10gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-10gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-10gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-loopback { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-10gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-loopback { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-10gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-10gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-no-optic { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-10gb-sfp-plus@'] .state-no-optic { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="193mm" height="35.4mm" viewBox="0 0 193 35.4">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-activity { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-down { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-error { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-initializing { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-initializing { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-link { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-loopback { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-loopback { animation: portrayal-blink 0.25s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-no-link { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-no-optic { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-no-optic { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-on { --led-color: #2f6fdb; }
    g[data-ref^='nokia/me6-400gb-qsfp-dd@'] .state-up { --led-color: #39b54a; }</style>
